record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

Additional transferable low-F contexts include DHPG absolute oral bioavailability 5.4 ± 1.6%, terfenadine <5% (and <2% in men), phenylephrine poor/low-transient oral bioavailability, and hydroxytyrosol 6.2 ± 1.1% in humans.

L3 batefenterol oral exposure data show that after 200 µg oral [14C]-batefenterol, parent batefenterol concentrations were non-quantifiable with pooled AUC0-t of 0.614 h·pgEq/mL, while total radioactivity AUC0-t was 387.8 pgEq·h/mL, indicating extensive first-pass metabolism and negligible parent oral exposure for a structurally related long-chain beta2 agonist.

L5 gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism records are for other molecules (noscapine, labetalol, salbutamol, silybin, mitoxantrone, propranolol) and provide no query-specific efflux or intestinal-metabolism evidence; C54 salbutamol P-gp data are inconclusive, C52 propranolol efflux is attributed to passive diffusion, and the other efflux records are not transferable to the query.

The only contradictory-direction card, C24, reports hydroxytyrosol as highly bioavailable in rats, but it is qualitative, rat-specific, and contradicted by the human L1 value of 6.2% in the same context.
